anchors.note: The CoolKey driver reads one crafted object body from the saved fake-card transcript into `new_obj_data`. Decoding the staged witness under `fuzz_get_chunk()`'s format yields a 70-byte V1 object payload that starts `01 00 00 01 00 90 00 30 b3 00 02 ... 00 00 01 00 01 00 00 00 03 ...`; those bytes later supply the class and key-type values on the crashing path.

unsigned long fixed_attributes = bebytes2ulong(object_head->fixed_attributes_values);
return coolkey_get_attribute_data_fixed(attr_type, fixed_attributes, attribute);
anchors.note: When `CKA_CLASS` is requested for the V1 object from step 0, bytes `90 00 30 b3` are converted to `fixed_attributes = 0x900030b3`. `coolkey_get_attribute_data_fixed(CKA_CLASS, ...)` then extracts `cka_class = 3` and returns the 4-byte class value `00 00 00 03`.
The class bytes from step 1 are converted into the scalar `obj_class = 3`, i.e. `CKO_PRIVATE_KEY`. This value controls the object-class switch in `sc_pkcs15emu_coolkey_init`.

Because step 2 produced `obj_class = CKO_PRIVATE_KEY`, execution enters the private-key case and requests `CKA_KEY_TYPE`. For the witness object from step 0, the explicit V1 integer attribute `00 00 01 00 01 00 00 00 03` supplies `key_type = 3`, i.e. `CKK_EC`, so the RSA default path is not taken.

Still in the private-key case, `obj_info` is bound to the stack `prkey_info` structure that will be passed into `sc_pkcs15emu_object_add()`. The ASan frame layout later shows this stack object occupying offsets `[7712,8152)`, so its extent is 440 bytes.

Root cause. On the private EC-key path, the code assigns the public-key PKCS#15 type `SC_PKCS15_TYPE_PUBKEY_EC` even though the data pointer remains `obj_info = &prkey_info`. The fix changes this specific enum constant to `SC_PKCS15_TYPE_PRKEY_EC`.

Class dispatch uses the misclassified `type = SC_PKCS15_TYPE_PUBKEY_EC` from step 5, so it takes the public-key case and sets `data_len` to `sizeof(struct sc_pkcs15_pubkey_info)` = 464. That 464-byte copy size matches the ASan-reported read size and already exceeds the 440-byte `prkey_info` source from step 4.

The function allocates a 464-byte destination and then copies 464 bytes from `data`, which still points at `prkey_info`. ASan reports the resulting `READ of size 464` here; since `prkey_info` ends at stack offset 8152, the copy reads 24 bytes past that object into the redzone and triggers the stack-buffer-overflow.
